prompt: Stage 3-2. Your next opponent's frontline is a 2-star 3-cost bruiser with a cleave that damages every unit adjacent to its target, and it walks straight at whichever of your units is closest. Your 3-cost tank holds the centre-left of your front row. Your second tank (a 2-star 2-cost) is on the bench. Place it so the cleave never hits two of your frontliners at once.
explanation:
The cleave is a clump punisher for frontlines. Two tanks side by side means every swing on one of them also hits the other, and your support on row 1 behind them takes it too. Splitting the tanks to opposite wings forces the bruiser to pick one side; it walks to the nearer tank, cleaves only that tank, and the other side of your board stays untouched while your carries shoot from the middle.

The far-left hex is also acceptable: what matters is that no two of your frontliners share an edge. What you must not do is fill the row 0 centre, which is where instinct puts a second tank and where the cleave does the most work.
principle: A frontline is spread the same way a backline is: two units that share an edge share the damage.
commonMistake: Building a wall in the middle of row 0. It looks solid and it feeds every area effect on the enemy frontline.
